sections.html:
• Scientific name: Hypostomus uruguayensis Reis, Weber & Malabarba, 1990
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2020)
  • Breeding: unreported

• Etymology: from Uruguay.

The Hypostomus genus has 7 soft rays in the dorsal fin, whereas the similar-looking Pterygoplichthys species have 10 soft dorsal fin rays.

South America: Uruguay River basin. Also recorded in the La Plata basin: Uruguay, Paraná (including Middle Paraná and Bermejo), Paraguay (including Pilcomayo, Upper Pilcomayo, and Upper Paraguay with the Cuiabá and Manso rivers). Type locality: Rio Uruguay at "Rancho da Amizade," São Borja, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
South America: Uruguay River basin (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Uruguay). Type locality: Rio Uruguay at "Rancho da Amizade", São Borja, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
Will need a good sized aquarium of 5 ft (150 cm) or over due to their final adult size.
As this genus in the main are messy eaters, good water quality and filtration would need to be adhered to.
Will eat all manner of foods in the aquarium: vegetable, tablet and pellet foods and a good quality flake food.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.
Etymology: Greek hypo = under + Greek stoma = mouth. The species name refers to the river in which the type specimen was collected.
IUCN Red List: despite the little information available on this species, it has a wide range and no apparent threats. Therefore, it is assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2023).
